Compute (1) Spearman(G_L,CPSC, G_L,PTB,std) over L8; (2) in each arm, Spearman(G_L, univariate OOF B1 AUC_L), with AUC computed on probabilities, not compute_f1_auc's binary AUC; (3) mapping-sensitivity reruns of G_PTB,raw and G_PTB,std at n=600, using scp_codes from ptbxl_database.csv and records within the 1357 only (B0 exists only there): (a) L8 primary; (b) L9 with STE as mapped; (c) L7 without STE and PAC; (d) NORM strict: positive only at likelihood 100 and exclusive, records with NORM+X dropped from evaluation; (e) RBBB := CRBBB or IRBBB for records among the 1357 carrying IRBBB; (f) STD broad = STD_ + ISC* + NST_ + DIG + INJ*. Weights are recomputed for each variant.
primary_analyses.decision_rule: H_label (concept difficulty) supported if Spearman(1) >= 0.6, the same labels (from STD, I-AVB, PAC) are among the top 3 gains in both arms, and Spearman(2) <= -0.5 in both arms. H_dom predicts a gain spread across labels on CPSC, including morphologically clear ones (AF, LBBB), with no PTB counterpart. Mapping artifact: if the PTB conclusion from P1/P2 changes category (as defined in P2) between variants (a) and (c)-(f), the PTB arm is declared mapping-sensitive. The domain conclusion is then limited to the labels where it is stable, and the label-definition (concept-shift) part of H_label is reported as not separable from domain.

secondary_analyses.computation: Per label and arm: univariate AUC of the own logit vs 5-fold OOF LR on the 9 logits (StratifiedGroupKFold by patient for PTB). Computed overall, with abnormal-only negatives (NORM-only records removed), and with P2 weights. Also a 2-feature model [own logit, mean of other 8 logits], the share frac = (2feat - own)/(S1 - own), and R2 of the row-mean logit on gold indicators.
secondary_analyses.purpose: Uses B1 only and does not depend on B0. Shows whether the cross-label suppression structure, and a per-image 'yes-bias' nuisance factor, exist in PTB once case mix matches CPSC. It separates H_prev from H_dom for component (c).

secondary_analyses.computation: For single-label records of gold class c: B1 response matrix R[c,A] = mean 1[P_A >= 0.5] and B0 response matrix Q[c,A] = mean 1[A in B0]. Report dR = R_CPSC - R_PTB and dQ with bootstrap CIs. For B0 also: OOV/empty rate, P(STD in B0 | gold AF without STD), P(NORM in B0 | gold abnormal), and predicted vs gold cardinality, each standardised to CPSC's class mix. Plus a domain classifier (y = PTB vs CPSC) on the 9 B1 logits within each gold class, balanced LR with 5-fold OOF AUC, recomputed under the P4 mapping variants.
secondary_analyses.purpose: Prevalence-free view of where the two sources differ. H_task predicts equal or larger prompt artifacts on PTB images. H_dom predicts broad class-conditional shift, including on LBBB and AF. Concept shift predicts shift concentrated on STD, STE and RBBB that shrinks under redefinition.

secondary_analyses.computation: For each arm and n, compute THR (per-label OOF threshold on raw P(yes), fallback 0.5) and B1@0.5 alongside S1. Split G = [B1@0.5 - B0] + [THR - B1@0.5] + [S1 - THR]. Also index the learning curves by median positives per label in the draw, and log fallback counts per label and n.
secondary_analyses.purpose: Shows whether in-domain gains need only re-thresholding, which would point to an operating-point or prior effect (H_task/H_prev), or need re-ranking. It also makes the curves comparable when rare-label positives differ by about 10x between arms.

secondary_analyses.computation: Fit S1 coefficients on the CPSC pool (600) and apply them to the PTB test, then the reverse direction (PTB pool -> CPSC test). For n in {50,100,200,600}, use the target's n labels to refit only the per-label intercept and threshold (or a Platt a,b fit on the transferred score), and compare with full S1 on the same draws. Report per-label test AUC of the transferred score, and the cosine similarity of standardized coefficient vectors.
secondary_analyses.purpose: If intercept-only adaptation of the source structure recovers most of the gain, the cross-label structure is model- or concept-level and the shift is prior-like (against H_dom). If only a full refit works, the structure is domain-specific.

secondary_analyses.computation: Run OCR with clarity/lead_locate.py:ocr (Apple Vision on CPU, not model inference) on all 1357 PTB images. Flags: has_measure (regex 'PR:|QRS|QT|Rate:') and has_demo ('Sex:|Age:'). Within PTB, for the strata with and without measurements: B1 per-label AUC, B0 F1 for I-AVB/LBBB/RBBB, and G_PTB(600) under the P1 protocol with a stratum x label bootstrap interaction. Also run the same checks on a random 50 CPSC images to confirm they carry no printed measurements.
secondary_analyses.purpose: Checks whether 'in-domain image' really means printed PR/QRS values that the model can read. If so, part of the PTB advantage is a text shortcut rather than appearance familiarity.

secondary_analyses.computation: Repeat P1 on PTB with a record-level random split and record-level inner CV. Report G_PTB(grouped) - G_PTB(random) with a CI.
secondary_analyses.purpose: Measures patient-leakage inflation of S1 in the PTB arm; CPSC has no patient IDs, so this cannot be checked there.

secondary_analyses.computation: Apply EM prior adjustment (clarity/transfer.py em_prior) to B1 using unlabeled target images in each arm, then threshold at 0.5, and also with THR thresholds from n labels. Report the share of G each recovers in CPSC, PTB-raw and PTB-weighted.
secondary_analyses.purpose: Measures the pure label-shift share of the gain (H_prev in its simplest form).

secondary_analyses.computation: Pool per-label rows: CPSC L8, PTB L8 (raw and weighted, kept separate) and CODE-15's 6 multi-label labels. Fit OLS G_aL ~ Delta_rank_aL + OOD_dummy + native_prompt_dummy + label fixed effects (shared labels AF, I-AVB/1dAVb, LBBB, RBBB), with a record-cluster bootstrap. Descriptive only: about 22 rows and one dataset per cell.
secondary_analyses.purpose: A cross-arm check of H_head. If Delta_rank alone accounts for G and the dummies are about 0, the arm differences run through B0's position relative to the probe ROC.

secondary_analyses.computation: Rescore B0 in each arm (a) with empty/OOV parses dropped from the evaluation and (b) with OOV superclass tokens mapped (MI/STTC -> STD/STE as appropriate, flagged as ad hoc). Report how much G changes.
secondary_analyses.purpose: Checks that B0's silent empty parses, which get no at-least-one rule unlike S1, do not drive G or the DiD.

secondary_analyses.computation: Report the 9-label official compute_f1_auc for B0, THR, S1@n and S1B0 (exploratory) in both arms, plus CPSC results under the old ZS_THR fallback, next to the new protocol.
secondary_analyses.purpose: Continuity with previously reported numbers (CPSC 57.6 / 68.8) and transparency about the protocol change.

protocol_details: Freeze: commit the analysis code (P0-P4 plus secondary analyses) and this plan, and record md5 hashes before computing any metric that uses PTB B0. Do not read outputs/pulse7b/ptbxl-cpsc9/answers.jsonl, except for a line count, until then. Disclose that reviewers saw 152-200 interim B0 answers, for error signatures only.

Data: PTB = 1357 records in data/derived/ptbxl_cpsc9.json, B1 = outputs/clarity/b1_ptbxl_all.jsonl, B0 = outputs/pulse7b/ptbxl-cpsc9/answers.jsonl, patient_id and scp_codes from data/ptbxl_meta/ptbxl_database.csv (ecg_id = number in the 'ptb-xl-<id>' record id). CPSC = all 2061 records of cpsc-test (data/splits/cpsc.json dev+test), B1 = b1_cpsc_dev/test.jsonl, B0 = outputs/pulse7b/cpsc-test/answers.jsonl.
Gold and B0 parsing: substring match over LABELS = [NORM, AF, I-AVB, LBBB, RBBB, PAC, PVC, STD, STE], exactly as in clarity/learning_curve.py. Do not split on ';'.

Primary metric: macro-F1 from scripts/score_ecgbench.py compute_f1_auc, with STE removed from gold and prediction lists (L8). Its returned 'AUC' is computed on binary predictions and is not used as ranking evidence; ranking AUCs use sklearn roc_auc_score on probabilities. Weighted analyses use a re-implementation checked against compute_f1_auc at w=1. Every L8 label must be present in each test fold, so the MultiLabelBinarizer macro does not silently drop a label.

Splits: 20 outer partitions per arm (seeds 0..19). PTB uses GroupShuffleSplit by patient_id: pool 600 records (patients added until 600 is reached), test = the remaining ~757. CPSC uses a random 600/1461 split. Redraw until every L8 label has >= 10 positives in pool and test; log the number of redraws.
n grid {25, 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 600}, with one draw per partition per n (seed 100*r + n). That gives 20 values per n per arm; at n=600 the draw is the whole pool.

Calibrator: per label, LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=2000) on the 9 B1 logits clipped at 1e-4. Threshold: F1-max over grid 0.02..0.96 step 0.01 on OOF probabilities from StratifiedGroupKFold(k=min(5,pos,neg), shuffle, random_state=r), grouped by patient for PTB. Fallback when pos<2 or neg<2: raw P(yes) >= 0.5 in both arms. ZS_THR is not used.

At-least-one rule: S1, THR and B1@0.5 always predict at least one label (argmax P_L/thr_L over all 9 labels), applied before STE is dropped. B0 is scored as generated (empty parse = no label); S9 gives a sensitivity check.
Case-mix weights (P2): fixed once from full-arm exact 9-label-set frequencies, with w=0 for PTB sets unseen in CPSC. Report ESS overall and per test fold. Sensitivity: cap 10, and merged strata.

Uncertainty: in each partition, a paired cluster bootstrap over test units (patients for PTB, records for CPSC), B=200, so 4000 pooled replicates per arm. Cross-arm contrasts pair replicates by shuffled index. Report 95% percentile CIs, the mean and SD across the 20 partitions, and the 2.5/97.5 percentiles of the partition distribution. Do not report counts of draws that beat B0 as significance.

Smallest effect of interest: 3 macro-F1 points. Decision thresholds as in P1-P4 (R_std <= 0.3 with upper CI < 0.5 for domain; R_std >= 0.6 with lower CI > 0.3 for case mix; otherwise partial or inconclusive). Per-label contrasts are secondary, with Holm correction over the 8 labels.
Confirmatory set = P1-P4 only. S1B0, S3 (evidence features), EM, CODE-15 cross-arm regression, OCR strata and all mapping variants are exploratory or sensitivity analyses and are labelled as such.

Compute: CPU only, read-only on existing outputs, plus the in-progress PTB B0 run. No other model inference. OCR with Apple Vision (lead_locate.ocr) is allowed because it is not model inference; S5 is dropped if it is unavailable.
limitations_to_state: One dataset per cell: CPSC (OOD image, new prompt), PTB (in-domain image, new prompt), CODE-15 (in-domain image, native prompt). There is no OOD-image + native-prompt cell, and nothing is replicated, so a dataset-specific quirk cannot be fully separated from 'domain'. The crossed prompt x image design and a second OOD source (G12/CSN) need new GPU generation and are out of scope.

'In-domain' PTB bundles several things: image appearance, PTB-XL annotation conventions and severity spectrum, the trained SCP vocabulary, and printed demographics or measurements on many renderings. With images alone, the PTB arm cannot separate covariate shift from concept or spectrum shift. Waveform measurements (ST amplitude, PR) are not used.

The CPSC-9 prompt reuses the PTB-XL superclass training template, so 'same prompt' does not mean equal novelty across image sources. The B1 yes/no probe is a new format in every arm, so S1 is never an in-domain readout.

PTB labels are mapped from SCP codes. STE is mostly injury codes (excluded from the primary metric). STD uses STD_ only, RBBB is CRBBB only, and NORM is non-exclusive and admits low likelihood. The 1357-record subset excludes 725 records with no mapped label, which removes look-alike negatives (IRBBB, LAFB, IVCD). Mapping variants are limited to records that have B0.

Case-mix reweighting relies on exact label-set strata with low ESS (about 280 overall, fewer in the test fold). PAC and other rare strata carry large weights, so P2 can be underpowered; a null there is reported as inconclusive, not as support for domain.

Rare labels are small in PTB: about 15-25 test positives for PAC, LBBB and RBBB, so per-label F1 SE is about 8-10 points. Learning curves at small n hit the fallback often, and cross-arm comparisons at equal n are not at equal positives per label.

CPSC records are 6-60 s but are rendered as one ~10 s page, so episodic labels (PAC, PVC, ST changes) may be off-screen. Record lengths are not available locally, so this headroom difference is not controlled.

Exclusion of PTB-XL fold 10 from ECGInstruct (including ECG-QA, which is built on PTB-XL) is not verified locally. If fold 10 was trained on, B0 and B1 on PTB are inflated and the domain effect is overstated.

CPSC has no patient IDs, so the CPSC arm cannot be patient-grouped. The previous CPSC learning curve used one fixed split and ZS_THR fallbacks tuned partly on PTB, so the protocol was changed. New CPSC numbers may differ slightly from 57.6/68.8.

The comparison is asymmetric by design: S1 always gets the at-least-one rule and target-label fitting, and B0 gets neither. 'Calibration gain' mixes readout quality, operating-point/prior adaptation and cross-label re-ranking; P3 reports these separately. Monotone recalibration alone (THR) did not help on CPSC.

Forking paths: the PTB experiment and estimand were chosen after seeing the CPSC and CODE-15 results, and interim B0 records were inspected. S1B0 was added post hoc and is exploratory. CODE-15's null mainly reflects that B0 is strong under its native prompt; it cannot by itself show that calibration fails in-domain.

_freeze.disclosure: Design reviewers saw ~150-200 interim PTB B0 answers (error signatures only). Analysis code was dry-run end-to-end on a DUMMY PTB B0 (all NORM) only; real PTB B0 answers were not read before this freeze.
_freeze.deviation: Fallback threshold 0.5 in both arms per P0(4); CPSC arm is re-run under the new 20-partition protocol (earlier CPSC numbers kept for continuity only).
